patch.value: Public SDK surface shape: 881 exports behind one flat entrypoint with no capability tiering and a 250ms eager import cost

Importing the published SDK entry yields 881 runtime exports from a single module (693 functions plus 188 values/classes), and package.json declares only four subpaths: '.', './sdk', './sdk/runtime', './sdk/testing'. Everything else — query, governance, graph, merge, test, extension, cli-contracts — is flattened into that one namespace, so a package author who needs one primitive loads the whole graph: 'import(dist/cli-bundle/sdk.js)' costs 289ms against a 41ms bare-node baseline, the same as importing the entire CLI (286ms). The namespace is also undifferentiated: stable authoring primitives sit beside per-command flag-contract constants (ACTIVITY_COMMANDER_STRING_OPTION_CONTRACTS, CALENDAR_FLAG_CONTRACTS, ...) with nothing marking which symbols are the supported authoring surface. src/sdk/index.ts is 35 'export *' lines, which is why the surface grows silently. Duplicate check: searched SDK surface/entrypoint/subpath/tiering/import-cost all-status. pm-e6tm5c owns the snapshot and breaking-change gate — it will freeze whatever shape exists, so shaping must precede or accompany it; pm-9x6e (closed) zeroed the private-core import baseline in the other direction; pm-ds3b (closed) documented the promoted primitives; pm-agou is the GA stability ADR; pm-feecbs governs external package conformance, not host export shape. None of them own how the surface is partitioned or what it costs to import.

The public SDK is partitioned into documented subpath entrypoints that mirror the internal module families (at minimum core item/query, governance, graph, merge, extension authoring, testing, and cli-contracts), each independently importable; a package author can import one family without loading the others, proven by a measured import-cost table in the repo showing per-entry cost against the bare-node baseline; the flat './sdk' entry keeps working unchanged as an aggregate so no existing consumer breaks; every export is classified as supported authoring surface, contract data, or advanced/internal-but-exported, and that classification is the input pm-e6tm5c snapshots; docs/SDK.md and the extension author docs route by entrypoint; no export is removed and no external package requires changes to keep working
Make building a pm package cheap to start and cheap to run: a small, tiered, independently loadable public API

The SDK is the product surface for the whole ecosystem; an 881-symbol flat namespace that costs a quarter second to import is both a discovery barrier for authors and a fixed latency cost in every extension process
pm-e6tm5c is about to turn the current shape into a frozen compatibility contract, and pm-9rgaal declares SDK-complete core as an outcome milestone — shaping after the freeze is a breaking change

value.text: Surface measurement: Object.keys on the published sdk entry yields 881 exports (693 functions, 188 values). src/sdk/index.ts is 35 'export *' lines, so any new module file joins the public surface with no review step. package.json exports declares four subpaths only ('.', './sdk', './sdk/runtime', './sdk/testing'); dist/sdk/index.d.ts carries 102 top-level export statements. Import cost measured against a 41ms bare-node baseline: sdk.js 289ms, main.js 286ms — importing one SDK primitive costs the same as launching the whole CLI. Contract constants (ACTIVITY_COMMANDER_STRING_OPTION_CONTRACTS, CALENDAR_FLAG_CONTRACTS, CONTEXT_FLAG_CONTRACTS and siblings) sit in the same namespace as authoring primitives with no marker distinguishing them.
